sanskrit_verse: त्रयः स्वतन्त्रा लोकेऽस्मिन् राजाचार्यस्तथैव च । प्रति प्रति च वर्णानां सर्वेषां स्वगृहे गृही ॥
transliteration: trayaḥ svatantrā loke 'smin rājācāryas tathaiva ca | prati prati ca varṇānāṃ sarveṣāṃ svagṛhe gṛhī ||
sph_interpretive_translation: In this world, three authorities are sovereign: the King, the Acharya, and the Grihapati of each respective varna.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is stratified by domain and dharma, not by force or delegation
Causation arises from svadharma-sustained roles within cosmic order
Capacity-based responsibility flows from self-realized sovereignty
Restoration logic requires alignment with one's intrinsic governing capacity
Consciousness alignment occurs through rightful autonomy in dharmic role
executable_legal_axioms: IF entity holds sovereign dharmic role THEN no external jurisdiction overrides internal svatantrya
IF dispute involves multiple svatantra entities THEN resolution must align with respective dharma domains
IF authority conflict arises THEN precedence follows proximity to Varnashrama-dharma alignment
IF grihastha exercises household sovereignty THEN king and acharya have no direct jurisdiction unless dharma is violated
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, this verse establishes that adjudication must recognize inherent sovereignty of the King (state), Acharya (spiritual guidance), and Grihapati (householder governance). Inter-jurisdictional conflicts are resolved by verifying alignment with respective svadharma rather than asserting hierarchical dominance.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramana is established through svatantrya-dharma correspondence. Anupurvasah manifests as sequential sovereignty: first self-governance (grihastha), then community (acharya), then state (raja). Responsibility is proportional to svatantrya. There is no punitive framework; misalignment results in natural consequence requiring realignment, not punishment.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate svadharma-realignment process for contested authority
Facilitate consciousness dialogue between conflicting svatantra entities
Reintegrate displaced sovereignty through dharma-based mediation
Restore integrity via acknowledgment of respective autonomous capacities
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands declared: Authority derives from svatantrya-dharma, not coercion. Justice restores alignment. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates.
